digest.component_or_area: MCP server error handling and CLI/library interface consistency
propositions: MCP tool failures currently emit unstructured prose in exception messages or ad-hoc partial shapes, lacking the machine error code discriminator that the CLI emits via error_envelope.
No single shared error vocabulary exists across library, CLI, and MCP interfaces; error codes are scattered string literals without a central classifier or registry.
A central error_code_for(exc)->str function and KNOWN_ERROR_CODES frozenset must be created in _errors.py to provide a single source of truth for all three interfaces.

MCP failures must be wrapped in McpEnvelopeError carrying a structured .envelope dict built via error_envelope(), deliverable as JSON in ToolError.__cause__, enabling agents to distinguish failure types (ticket_not_found vs concurrency_conflict vs gate refusal) without pattern-matching English.

The two existing ad-hoc MCP soft-error returns (_mcp_reads explain_criterion {error,kind}; _mcp_llm {error,resolution_class,...}) must be migrated to emit vocabulary error codes while preserving agent-branching fields.

TicketNotFoundError must be introduced as a ReadError subclass, raised only at genuine not-found sites (reads.py:310/313), enabling isinstance-based classification independent of human message text, while leaving the CLI message-keyed distinction (deps_failed vs ticket_not_found) byte-identical.
